summary: A 60-ft Aermotor fire tower in Wharton State Forest, first erected at Big Hill in 1938 and moved here in 1950; fenced off in 2016 after vandalism.

facts.design: 60-ft Aermotor tower with a metal box cab at the top, painted red and white

access.note: Fenced off on September 10, 2016 after vandalism. Wikipedia says visitors may enter when staff are present and by appointment; Atlas Obscura said in July 2017 it was not possible to visit.

visit.trail_note: The hill lies along the Batona Trail in Wharton State Forest

events.note: Original cupola lookout on the hill, built about 1912 per the NHLR; Atlas Obscura says a lookout has been there since about 1912
1914 newspapers conflict: the Inquirer says a lookout tower has been erected, while the Transcript says the state was still planning one
Tower first stood at Big Hill in 1938, per the NHLR
Moved from Big Hill to Apple Pie Hill
Closed to public access by a fence around the tower on September 10, 2016, due to vandalism

corrections.proposed: 1938 at Big Hill; relocated to Apple Pie Hill in 1950
corrections.why: The NHLR says the tower first stood at Big Hill in 1938 and was moved to Apple Pie Hill in 1950. The 1950 date is the move, not the first erection.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR and Atlas Obscura date a cupola lookout to about 1912. The 1914 newspapers describe a tower as erected (Inquirer) and as still planned (Transcript). We keep 1912 for the first lookout and report the 1914 conflict in the story.
Wikipedia says the tower is open with staff present and by appointment; Atlas Obscura, as of July 2017, says it was not possible to visit. We record restricted access and report both statements.

The NHLR names the New Jersey Forest Fire Service as administrator. Wikipedia and Eastern US Lookouts describe the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection closing access in 2016. Both are reported.

notes_for_editor: The brief's 1950 build year is the move date; the register says the tower first stood at Big Hill in 1938. The nj.com article on the 2016 closure returned HTTP 403 and was not read. The 1914 newspaper text is quoted through Eastern US Lookouts, not the original papers. Wikipedia gives the hill as 205 feet tall, while the NHLR and the NJ tower table give the tower site at 179 feet (55 m). No source found on current staffing. The NJ Forest Fire Service remains the register's administrator even though the state DEP closed the access in 2016.
